title: Close a named handwheel valve and lock it with a rotating valve cover and a padlock
instruction: Close gate valve V-21, the one with the yellow tag: turn its handwheel clockwise, seen from above, until it stops, about one full turn; let go and grip again as often as you need. Slide the red valve cover onto that handwheel from the side, open side first, so the stem sits in the middle of the cover, then swing the cover's loose half round until its ear lies on the other half's ear. Put your padlock's shackle through the inner holes of both ears and snap it shut. Do not touch valve V-23, the one with the green tag.
context: Isolating a line for maintenance means closing its valve and locking it closed. A handwheel has no lock hole, so it is enclosed in a lockout cover that is padlocked shut; closing the wrong valve, or leaving the cover unpadlocked, lets the line be reopened onto a worker.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top. Pipe run: a 1/2 in schedule-40 steel pipe (21.3 mm outside diameter, 48 cm long) runs left-right, its axis 26 cm in front of the bases and 5.5 cm above the table, from 12 cm right to 36 cm left of the midline, fixed to the table on two grey plastic stands (3 x 2 cm columns on 8 x 5 x 0.8 cm feet) at 9 cm right and 33 cm left of the midline. Valves: two Milwaukee Valve UP148 1/2 in bronze gate valves (body 51 mm end to end), stems vertical and 26 cm in front of the bases: V-21 on the midline, V-23 25 cm left of it. Each has a dark grey malleable iron handwheel (50.8 mm across, 6 mm round rim, four spokes, 90 g) whose rim is 15 cm above the table, its wheel nut's top 16 cm. Both valves are one full turn open; turned clockwise seen from above, a wheel stops at its seat after one turn. Valve tags: each valve has an engraved two-ply plastic tag (102 x 51 x 1.6 mm, letters about 28 mm tall) on an 8 mm steel strap clamped round the pipe 7.5 cm left of its stem: V-21's is yellow with black letters, V-23's green with white letters. Tag centre 9.5 cm behind the stem, 2 cm left of it and 14 cm above the table, long side left-right, face tilted back 60 degrees from vertical toward the robot. Lockout cover: a Master Lock 480 rotating gate valve lockout (red thermoplastic drum, 86 mm across and 41 mm deep outside, 30 mm deep inside, 19 mm stem opening in its back face, about 105 g; a fixed piece with an open sector and a loose piece that pivots at the centre and, opened, nests inside it; each piece has a flat padlock ear in the plane of its back face, 16 mm wide, reaching 76 mm from the centre, with two 9 mm holes 56 and 67 mm from the centre). It lies opened, back face down, on a grey plastic stand (4.5 x 4.5 cm, 8 cm tall, on a 7 x 7 cm foot) 13 cm in front of the bases and 13 cm right of the midline, its ears pointing at the robot and its open sector facing left. Padlock: a Master Lock 410 Zenex safety padlock (purple, 410PRP; body 38 x 45 x 19 mm, 6.35 mm steel shackle with 38 mm vertical and 20 mm horizontal clearance; 0.10 kg) stands upright and open (shackle popped up 16 mm, key in the cylinder) on a grey plastic column (1.0 x 1.2 cm, 11.3 cm tall, on a 5 x 5 x 1 cm foot) 14 cm in front of the bases and 14 cm left of the midline, legs side by side left-right, the short leg on the right. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0 if, at any time, V-23's handwheel turns 10 degrees or more, or V-21's, once closed, goes back more than 30 degrees from its seat before the after-release check. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if V-21's handwheel has turned 90 degrees or more toward closed; 0.5 if it is closed (within 10 degrees of its seat); 0.75 if, with the valve closed, the cover is fitted on V-21's handwheel (its centre within 6 mm of the stem, resting on the wheel nut within 5 mm of its fitted height, tilted less than 8 degrees) with its loose half swung shut (ears within 3 degrees of lined up); 1.0 if, in addition, the padlock is shut with its shackle through the inner holes of both ears and the after-release check passes. Dropping the padlock or the cover is not penalised by itself. After-release check, done once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the padlock and from V-21's stem for 2 s: pull the loose half's ear toward open with a spring scale at 15 N (55 mm from the centre, holding the fixed half's ear the other way) and keep pulling; after 2 s also turn the whole cover by its ear 30 degrees toward open (counterclockwise from above) over 2 s; then pull the cover straight up at 10 N for 2 s. Pass if the loose half stays within 10 degrees of shut, V-21's handwheel within 10 degrees of its seat, the cover's centre within 15 mm of the stem and no more than 25 mm above its fitted height (its back face stops under the wheel rim about 17 mm up), and the shackle is still through both ears; if not, the score is 0.75. Wheel angles are read against paint marks on the rim and the bonnet (under the cover, checked once it is removed after the trial); the loose half's angle from a photo taken from above with a protractor template.
reset_notes: Open the padlock with its key and remove it; swing the cover's loose half open, slide the cover off V-21's wheel and lay it back open on its stand, ears toward the robot; turn V-21's handwheel one turn counterclockwise from its seat (paint marks line up again); check V-23 is at its mark; stand the open padlock back on its column, short leg on the right. About 2 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, arms with the station's i2rt gains. The lock is geometry: wheel enclosed by the cover's faces and rims, shackle through both stacked ears. Wheel friction 0.3 N·m: real torque unpublished; the station gripper slipped on the 6 mm rim at 0.5. Stem rise not modelled; cover internals and mass inferred from photos; padlock latches by a catch, no key; check loads applied in sim, the turn as a set speed. Details in README.
